cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Shaping and forming processes change the shape of material without removing it; they rely on plastic deformation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Bending and folding shape sheet metal using a press brake; the bend angle, radius and material thickness are key variables.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Press forming (stamping) uses a punch and die to shape sheet metal in a single stroke; suitable for high-volume production.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Punching and blanking cut shapes from sheet metal using a press: punching removes a hole; blanking cuts out the entire shape.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Sand casting uses a sand mould to produce metal castings; suitable for low-volume, large or complex ferrous parts.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Pressure die casting forces molten metal into a steel mould (die) under high pressure; used for high-volume non-ferrous parts (zinc, aluminium, magnesium).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Injection moulding forces molten thermoplastic into a steel mould; the dominant process for high-volume polymer components.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Forging shapes heated metal by hammering or pressing; produces parts with excellent grain structure and strength.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Composite lay-up (hand lay-up or vacuum bagging) shapes fibre-reinforced polymers in moulds; used for large composite structures.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Bend allowance calculations account for material stretching on the outside of a bend and compression on the inside.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Tolerances and surface finish vary: die casting gives good finish and accuracy; sand casting gives a rougher surface and wider tolerances.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Shaping, Forming & Casting
cards.back: Draft angles (1-3 degrees) are needed on casting and moulding walls so the part can be removed from the mould.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — shaping, forming & casting?
cards.back: 1. For Shaping, Forming & Casting questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Shaping, Forming & Casting through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
